stem: A bank offers a nominal annual interest rate of 12% compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate (EAR)?  [Given: (1.01)^12 = 1.1268]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Treating the nominal 12% as if it were already the effective rate ignores the monthly compounding effect; the actual return is higher than 12%.
Using semi-annual compounding (1 + 0.12/2)^2 - 1 = 1.0609 - 1 = 6.09% per half-year or 12.36% annualised is the wrong period conversion for monthly compounding.
Subtracting nominal rate from 1 before applying the compounding formula gives a garbled value of roughly 11.32%; this is not a valid procedure.

explanation: The effective annual rate converts a nominal rate compounded m times per year into its true annual equivalent using EAR = (1 + r/m)^m - 1. Here r = 0.12 and m = 12 gives (1.01)^12 - 1 = 12.68%.

explanation_sections.punchline: Monthly compounding makes the true annual return 12.68%, not 12% - the compounding frequency inflates the effective rate.
explanation_sections.lesson: The effective rate always exceeds the nominal rate when compounding is more frequent than once per year.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Direct plug-in once you identify m = 12. Trap: option 1 = nominal rate, not effective rate.
